answer: Inter-arrival jitter gate. Each identity must keep its request inter-arrival times inside a per-class band; variance outside the band (too smooth, too bursty) gets throttled. A shale of paced, human-like gaps is learned from aggregate traffic, not individual histories. Crossing the ledge—sustained out-of-band timing—forces a slow re-admission queue costing roughly 40 minutes of idle wall-clock per identity per day. To forge many identities cheaply, an attacker must either pay that idle time across every sock puppet or emit detectable timing regularity.
